The 0.5.x names

Source: R/compat_names.R, R/compat_s3.R
rmbl-aliases.Rd

1.0.0 renamed most functions rmoriebricklayer 0.5.13 exported. The old names are no longer R functions, except the eleven rmoriedata 0.3.x calls (rmbl-compat) and the S3 generics rate(), rate_change(), share() and yoy_summary(), which stay so methods written for them still dispatch. The command line knows every old name, from inst/compat/compat_names_map.tsv:


rmbl describe admissions
    what admissions() became, then the page of admits()
rmbl run admissions --adp 120 --alos 30
    call it by the old name, old arguments and values translated
rmbl migrate analysis.R
    show the 1.0.0 rewrite of a 0.5.x script; --write writes it

(blcli() runs the same verbs from R.) An option set under its 0.5.x name (rmoriebricklayer.xmss_index_file, rmoriebricklayer.data_cache ...) is read when the new name is not set.

Details

The four generics return their result in its 0.5.x form: the 0.5.x column and field names (nested tables and attributes too; the last table lists them) and, for a delimited writer, the 0.5.x header. Such a result carries the class rmbl_old in front, so print(), format(), plot(), summary() and the generics read it in the 1.0.0 names. A 1.0.0 call is never translated. yoy() kept its name: it returns the 0.5.x names when called with a 0.5.x argument name, and the 1.0.0 names otherwise.

Renamed allowed values

Old name, argument, then each old value and the value it is translated to.


analyse_table              direction  higher_is_better -> higher,
                                      lower_is_better -> lower
crf_no2                    outcome    all_cause_mortality -> allcause,
                                      childhood_asthma -> chiast
crf_pm25                   outcome    all_cause_mortality -> allcause
pollution_burden           outcome    all_cause_mortality -> allcause,
                                      childhood_asthma -> chiast
pollution_burden_by_area   outcome    all_cause_mortality -> allcause,
                                      childhood_asthma -> chiast
survey_design              type       mean_bootstrap -> meanboot
verify_pollution           outcome    all_cause_mortality -> allcause,
                                      childhood_asthma -> chiast

Examples

# what a 0.5.x name became, and its 1.0.0 help page (the first lines)
out <- character()
blcli(c("describe", "admissions"), out = function(...) {
  out <<- c(out, paste0(...))
})
cat(head(strsplit(paste(out, collapse = ""), "\n")[[1]], 3), sep = "\n")
#> admissions() is the 0.5.x name of admits() (renamed in 1.0.0)
#> Admissions implied by a population and a length of stay
#> 
# the generics kept their names, and return their result under the 0.5.x
# names
r <- rate(c(5, 12), population = c(1000, 4000))
names(r)
#> [1] "count"      "population" "rate"       "lower"      "upper"     
#> [6] "flag"      
rate_change(
  data.frame(year = 2023:2024, n = c(10, 14), pop = 1000),
  count = "n",
  population = "pop",
  period = "year"
)
#> ╭── Change in rate per 1,000 ─────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Count       n                                                         │
#> │   Population  pop                                                       │
#> │   Period      year                                                      │
#> │   Lag         1                                                         │
#> │   Interval    95% exact conditional, on the % change                    │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   year  count  population  rate  precnt  prepop  prerate  rateratio     │
#> │   ----  -----  ----------  ----  ------  ------  -------  ---------     │
#> │   2023     10       1,000    10                                         │
#> │   2024     14       1,000    14      10   1,000       10      1.400     │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   year  pctchg  pct_interval    flag                                    │
#> │   ----  ------  --------------  ----                                    │
#> │   2023                          [1]                                     │
#> │   2024   40.00  [-42.2, 252.3]                                          │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   Not distinguishable from 0 (interval includes it): 2024 (+40.0%).     │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   [1] no comparison period                                              │
#> │   pctchg is the percentage change in the rate from the period `lag`     │
#> │   before; an interval that includes 0 means the change could be chance. │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
share(c(a = 3, b = 7))
#> ╭── Share ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Count     count                                                     │
#> │   Total     10                                                        │
#> │   Interval  95% Wilson                                                │
#> │                                                                       │
#> │   label  count  total  share  95% CI                                  │
#> │   -----  -----  -----  -----  --------------                          │
#> │   a          3     10     30  [10.78, 60.32]                          │
#> │   b          7     10     70  [39.68, 89.22]                          │
#> │                                                                       │
#> │   Highest share: row 2 (70); lowest: row 1 (30). Their intervals      │
#> │   overlap: the data cannot tell the two apart.                        │
#> │                                                                       │
#> │   Each share is the count as a percentage of the total, with a Wilson │
#> │   interval, which stays inside 0 to 100 for small counts.             │
#> ╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
y <- yoy(
  data.frame(year = 2021:2024, n = c(10, 12, 9, 15)),
  value = "n",
  period = "year"
)
yoy_summary(y)
#> ╭── Year-over-year summary ──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Series  1                                                            │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   from  to    first  last  totalpct  cagrpct  periods  up  down  flat  │
#> │   ----  ----  -----  ----  --------  -------  -------  --  ----  ----  │
#> │   2021  2024     10    15        50    14.47        4   2     1     0  │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   totalpct is the change from the first period to the last and cagrpct │
#> │   the compound rate per step; up, down and flat count the changes from │
#> │   one period to the next.                                              │
#> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
